mapping.public_requirements: overview.md:3,9; instruction.md opening-state and examples paragraphs

atomic_outcomes.outcome: Useful starting source automatically produces preview and console output without Run.
A chosen built-in example supplies editable source and working output; an authored edit actually executes.
The edited example saves as a separate exact user record; reloading the built-in example preserves its original filename/source.
JS and complete HTML execute in the mode selected by filename alone. Lowercase fallback isolates case handling.
CSS applies to a fresh copy of the last successful document, preserving its content and prior authored style.
Uppercase .JS, .HTML and .CSS dispatch correctly without selecting a separate language.

After the observed prior document, the later JS Run produces its own fresh-undefined preview and fresh-js-log without the old heading. Global freshness also requires S04's executed A setter/start and B DOM/log showing typeof window.__cancelLeak is undefined; cancellation timing need not pass.

After the S02 control script and button handler have actually produced their markers, CSS retains that document and its visible enabled button. The permitted HTML or fallback JS control is valid. An ordinary click on that retained button succeeds as a browser action, but neither old marker count increases during CSS Run or the click. A removed, blank, hidden or disabled button cannot establish inert copying. CSS colour/style correctness is scored separately.

The positively observed authored oldGlobal is absent in the matched current CSS execution state, before any later JS Run. Use the actual realm/lifecycle rule; unavailable matching is the named permitted-observation incomplete branch, never assumed absence or an architecture defect.

After the matching button timer really fires once, a second observed pending timer is replaced by CSS before due. The last-good CSS document remains and no second callback DOM/log/success arrives through the stated window; ordinary execution recovers. Other CSS outcome verdicts are not prerequisites.
After each six-second idle interval, the completed preview handles the click and later focused key/input without rerunning source.

After a completed preview and at least one of its authored handlers actually works, Stop reports stopped, prevents further old-handler output and permits a new Run. Removed/static/disabled controls after Stop are valid.
B supersedes genuinely pending A: A's delayed output, DOM and success never become current. Fresh globals are owned by S02.
Stop reports cancellation, prevents the active timer's late output and permits a new Run. Rollback is separate.
Stopping the active timer retains/restores B's completed render; provisional candidate display is optional.
All four parent-document/storage operations are blocked, actual host state is unchanged, and own-document execution remains usable.

Healthy controls succeed and all nine candidates reach S06's accepted denial/no-content/fallback/public-role outcomes. A confirmed exposure is a local no. Only the narrowly defined unresolved public-role observation or failed evaluator tooling uses EVALUATION_INCOMPLETE; neither can simultaneously be an exposure verdict.
With matching transport controls, separate fetch/Image runs visibly refuse access with no extra deliveries/content; ordinary execution recovers.
The HTML control's ordinary strings/comments/text containing unsupported-family words renders and logs successfully.
Each of the five separate unsupported-family probes is clearly refused, preserves the good render and permits ordinary recovery.
Both literal loops terminate within the allowed budget margin with a time-limit reason, early logs preserved and successful recovery.
Each loop timeout retains/restores recorded currentLastGood rather than a failed or empty candidate.
The console identifies the not-a-function error involving forEeach.
The error identifies line 4 of the exact entered JS source, without wrapper offsets.
The JS failure restores recorded currentLastGood, not failed-partial-dom; an ordinary recovery Run works.
The console identifies undefinedFunctionCall from the complete HTML source.
The error identifies line 6 of the exact complete HTML document, including its markup.
The HTML failure restores recorded currentLastGood, not Failed HTML candidate; an ordinary recovery Run works.
The timer callback's thrown async-error-marker is reported as a failure.
The timer error identifies entered user-source line 2.
The timer failure restores recorded currentLastGood, not async-failed-candidate; an ordinary recovery Run works.
The unhandled promise-error-marker rejection is reported as a failure.
The unhandled rejection identifies entered user-source line 2.
The rejection restores recorded currentLastGood, not promise-failed-candidate; an ordinary recovery Run works.
The four authored console levels have their exact values, order and unambiguous level indicators; console.error alone is a log.
App controls expose object properties, nested deep value and array elements rather than opaque summaries.
Previously observed log entries remain while subsequent Runs actually append their distinct new markers, until Clear is used.
The completed Run shows a measured duration, not a blank or placeholder.
New rows follow at the bottom; when deliberately scrolled up, incoming rows preserve the reading position.
Ordinary Clear removes prior rows; unrelated duration/status labels may remain.
Enabled Auto-run waits for a typing pause, resets its wait on closer-spaced edits, then executes only the final version within about two seconds.

First observe an authored edit execute automatically with Auto-run on and no manual Run. Then edits made with Auto-run already off remain unexecuted throughout the measured-delay-plus-margin window, and deliberate Run executes that exact pending source. A dead Auto-run feature cannot pass; correct debounce-reset behaviour is not a prerequisite.

After observing an authored edit execute automatically with Auto-run on, disable it before a further edit's measured debounce expires. That queued edit stays unexecuted for the full observation window and then executes through deliberate Run. A dead Auto-run feature cannot pass; correct debounce-reset behaviour is not a prerequisite.
Ordinary Run executes authored code with Auto-run both on and off; the on-state proof has no pending edit debounce.
Dividers change editor/preview and preview/console allocations while the panes remain usable.
The changed allocations survive reload; no exact pixels or layout are prescribed.
The populated editor uses a monospaced face.
The editor displays actual line numbers for entered source.
JS, complete HTML and CSS each have visible syntax colouring under their corresponding filenames.
A cursor beside either brace visibly identifies the matching pair.
Tab consistently indents all three selected lines without changing source. Retaining selection is not required.
Shift+Tab removes a consistent indent from all three selected lines. Reselect/manual-indent if needed to isolate this action.
New drafts save as distinct exact records; loading restores each one's fields. S23's current Save updates its existing identity rather than adding another.
Both saved identities and exact fields remain retrievable after browser reload.
The one process restart preserves recorded identities/fields/revisions exactly once; a current post-restart Save changes only its target and persists.
An otherwise-valid stale Save is refused with newer fields/revision unchanged. The successful newer Save is its control; S21 owns update fidelity.
The actual dirty editor gets useful conflict feedback, retains all unsaved fields and supports deliberate latest-revision recovery; proactive prevention is valid.
Padded unused titles are stored/displayed trimmed after both creation and rename.
Current rename changes only the selected title, preserving its filename/source and the complete sibling record.

With an observed successful valid current title write and unused-title recovery, UI and current-revision server writes refuse exact/padded collisions with useful feedback and both complete records/revisions unchanged.
With an observed successful valid current title write and unused-title recovery, otherwise-valid empty and whitespace-only titles are refused without saved-state mutation.
A case-distinct title coexists under its own identity and exact fields.

An otherwise-valid stale rename is usefully refused without newer-record mutation; actual current renames before/after work. A request replay can establish this server outcome independently of dirty-editor retention.

The actual old-revision editor retains its exact dirty title/filename/source with useful conflict or deliberate prevention feedback, then supports deliberate latest/reapply/current-Save readback. Replay alone cannot prove retention; no particular recovery control is required.
Duplicate creates a distinct stable identity with its chosen title and the original exact filename/source.
Each own edit actually saves and reloads: changing Original preserves Copy's previous source, and then changing Copy preserves Original's independently saved source.
Duplicate/create refuses the existing copy title without overwrite or extra same-title record; a new unused title succeeds.
Delete asks first, and cancellation leaves the complete library and exact records unchanged after reload.
The actual confirmed removal deletes only the selected identity durably, preserving sibling/unrelated records. Confirmation availability is separately owned.

An otherwise-valid stale delete is usefully refused without newer-record mutation; actual current deletes before/after work. Replay can establish this server outcome independently of dirty-editor retention. Confirmation is not scored here.

The actual old-revision editor retains its exact dirty title/filename/source with useful conflict or deliberate prevention feedback, then supports deliberate latest/reapply/current-Save readback. Replay alone cannot prove retention; no particular recovery control is required.
Updating the removed identity is usefully refused without resurrection, replacement or unrelated mutation; an existing-record update works.
The edited record is identifiable and source-only, title-only and filename-only changes each show unsaved state.
Each of four replacement routes warns, and cancellation preserves all dirty fields. Re-establish each fixture independently.
Accepting each replacement reaches its actual destination, while discarded edits never change saved Base. No new-draft template is prescribed.
Dirty work gets native leave protection: dismiss retains the draft, accept permits reload, saved data stays intact; clean reload does not warn.
An actual unsaved-draft export downloads the exact filename and unchanged source, not merely a toast.

Each lowercase .js, .html and .css import supplies its exact filename/source in an editable draft; its own-language edit is saved and reloaded under the recorded identity. Execution and case-handling verdicts are separate.

After the supported file actually appears in the draft, its authored markers remain unexecuted and the recorded successful preview remains for the off-state window; deliberate Run then produces that same imported source's DOM/log markers.
After the same importer has actually accepted a supported control file, an unsupported import gets useful refusal while the current title, filename and source remain unchanged.

With an observed valid supported-filename write and successful valid recovery, an otherwise-valid current server write refuses unsupported.txt without field/revision mutation. A lowercase control is valid.

With an observed valid supported-filename write and successful valid recovery, an otherwise-valid current server write refuses nested/demo.js without field/revision mutation. A lowercase control is valid.
The actual importer accepts supported .JS, .HTML and .CSS files with exact filename/source. Server acceptance is independently scored.
Otherwise-valid current writes accept and persist .JS, .HTML and .CSS filenames unchanged. Use an independent lowercased/imported or ordinary draft if uppercase import failed.
The control switches chrome, editor and console into both actual appearances; either may be the starting theme.
During two actually observed theme changes, the recorded exact draft fields and existing successful preview/console output remain intact. Preview recolouring is not required.
The discoverable documented Run binding alone produces keyboard-marker and keyboard-log without clicking Run.
The discoverable documented Save binding alone saves the exact draft fields without clicking Save.
The discoverable documented Clear binding alone removes prior rows without clicking Clear.
After the four-second callback actually emits late-callback-entered, it shares the original Run budget: timely termination/reason, no resumption and successful recovery; no fresh callback clock.
The timed-out callback retains/restores recorded currentLastGood rather than failed-loop-candidate; provisional display is optional.
After a successful interaction commits interaction-committed, the later failure retains/restores that state, not initial or provisional/late DOM.
Later accepted, ignored or blocked input cannot extend the pending interaction's budget; timeout/reason, no late resumption and ordinary recovery are observed.

scope: Current row identities/descriptions and exact unchanged original scenario budgets. Mapping is not evidence that every public behavior is observed or that all outcomes are independent.
